Inflationary is intensifying in Japan:

Japan’s Services Producer Price Index (SPPI) jumped +4.2% YoY in October, its largest annual increase since 1990, and far above expectations of +3.6%.

This index tracks domestic prices businesses charge each other for services, and serves as a key inflation metric in Japan.

MoM, the index rose +1.1%, up from +0.3% in the previous month and marking its biggest monthly increase in 6 months.

The latest surge was driven particularly by higher ocean freight transportation costs, leasing costs, and hotel charges.

Prices in transport and postal activities alone jumped +9.4% YoY in October, following an +8.4% increase in September.

Rising inflationary pressures are strengthening the case for a December rate hike by the Bank of Japan.

BREAKING: The Nasdaq 100 has recorded an average intraday range of 3.8% over the last 5 trading sessions, its highest 5-day volatility since April 2025.

This is also its 2nd-highest reading since the 2022 bear market, when it peaked at 4.0%.

Elon Musk on what led him to start SpaceX:

"I mistakenly thought that the reason that we're not sending people to Mars was because we'd lost the will to explore or something... And I thought, 'Well, maybe that needs to be reignited.'"

"I came up with this idea to do basically a philanthropic mission to Mars with 100% probability of losing all the money, in order to reignite interest in that goal. But after a while I realized that was actually a mistake."

"The United States is a nation of explorers... I think, more than any other country, [it] is a distillation of the human spirit of exploration."

"There's no lack of will. But people need to believe that there's a way, and a way that's feasible and that it's not going to bankrupt the country, and their living standard won't be materially affected. And then I think they're super, super keen on that goal."

@elonmusk at the Los Angeles World Affairs Council, 2013

Ben Horowitz on why asking whether AI is good or bad misses the point:

"I always like to go back to a quote from Andy Grove, which I absolutely love, which he said in the '90s. And somebody asked him, 'Andy, is the microprocessor good or bad?' And he said, 'Well, that's not even the right question. That's like asking, is steel good or bad? It is. And so it's our job to make it good.'"

"You can't get rid of the wheel now. It's over. It's here. You can't get rid of AI now. It's over. It's here. You can't outlaw math."

"So then the real question is, what do we have to do to make it good and positive for society? And by the way, without new technologies, how are we going to deal with pandemics or climate change or any of the real issues facing the world?"

@bhorowitz with @eriktorenberg on Turpentine VC, 2023

BREAKING: US new home sales jumped +14.2% MoM in October, to an annualized rate of 701,000 units, the highest since December 2025, crushing expectations of a -3.8% decline.

This marks the largest monthly increase since November 2025 and the 2nd-largest since August 2022.

It also marks a sharp recovery from the -9.7% MoM decline in September.

October's surge was driven by sales in the South, the nation's largest home-selling region, which soared +36.2% MoM, to an annualized rate of 515,000 units, the highest since March 2021.

At the same time, the median new home sale price fell -0.3% MoM and -3.2% YoY, to $391,300, the 2nd-lowest reading since July 2021.

Since the October 2022 peak, the median new home sale price has declined by $69,000, or -15.0%.

New home prices are falling sharply.

The Nasdaq dropped 4.6% before 10 AM, then clawed almost all of it back to close down just 0.62%.

A full panic and a full recovery in a single session. This is the millisecond market, where algorithms price every headline in a blink and the move is over before most investors can even reposition. Algorithmic trading is now 60 to 73% of US equity volume.

The old playbook of waiting for the dust to settle breaks when the session low and high are 4.4% apart. Our positioning model has CTA and vol-control exposure in the bottom 3% of its history, the same zone as the 2022 and April 2025 lows. The sellers are running low on ammo.

tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
The problem with predicting the bottom is that the price is already up by 25% or more.

Based on my dictionary, the bottom is in place if it gives the following sequence

Low, High, higher low, lower high, and finally a new high.
subtle variation
Low, High, higher low, higher-high

Look at $SOXX chart; the sequence that we got is:
Low, High, higher low, lower high, and then lower-low

We are still in the process of a downtrend
And when you are trading counter-trend, you need to be familiar with the rules of engagement

Overnight risk is real; sizing and cushion help navigate
